title: CertResult cert_file/key_file leaked in ssl_servername_cb (per-handshake leak)
label: FP
reason: The missing free of result.cert_file/result.key_file is real, but ssl_servername_cb returns early once chrooted or logged in (tls.c:61-62) and each accepted connection is handled in a forked child that exits (ftpd.c:5381-5393), so the allocation is reclaimed at child exit and cannot accumulate within a serving process. Only a bounded per-connection robustness leak remains; no security-relevant path is shown.

title: Missing checknamesanity/simplify on NLST/MLSD/MLST/MDTM/SIZE paths
label: TP
reason: With -X, dot_read_ok is set to 0 and RETR/CWD enforce checknamesanity, but NLST/MLSD/MLST call chdir()/modernformat() and MDTM/SIZE call stat() on the client-supplied path without that check. An authenticated user can therefore enumerate dot directories and stat dot files that -X is intended to hide.

title: Unsigned sentinel for user_quota_size misclassifies file-count-only quota as exceeded
label: FP
reason: The sentinel/off_t conversion can indeed mark a file-count-only quota as exceeded, but the condition only adds a rejection (overflow=1) for the legitimate configured user; it cannot permit a quota bypass or cross any privilege/confidentiality boundary. The report itself states there is no quota bypass, OOB, or privilege escalation, so this is a fail-closed functionality/availability defect with no attacker-controlled security path.

title: NULL crypto passed to strcasecmp in MySQL/PGSQL backends when MYSQLCrypt/PGSQLCrypt is unset
label: TP
reason: crypto is a zero-initialized file-scope pointer and the Crypt option is optional; pw_mysql_parse()/pw_pgsql_parse() only validate server/socket. A backend config without MYSQLCrypt/PGSQLCrypt therefore leaves crypto NULL, and a login that returns a DB row reaches strcasecmp(NULL, ...), crashing the authentication child (fail-closed remote DoS).

title: PureDB IPv6 allow/deny IP rules are silently discarded, bypassing per-user deny lists
label: TP
reason: pure-pw writes IP-rule text verbatim into a ':'-delimited PureDB record and pure_strtok2 splits on every ':'. An IPv6 literal such as ::1/128 therefore produces empty allow/deny fields (the shifted fragment lands after the time field), and access_ip_check() treats the empty deny list as permitting access, so the configured per-user IPv6 deny rule is never enforced.

title: Uninitialized stack memory disclosed in EPRT IPv6 error reply
label: TP
reason: do_ipv6_port declares struct sockaddr_storage a without zeroing it, and generic_aton() on success fills only ss_family and the 16 address bytes. When the supplied address differs from the peer, doport2() passes the structure to getnameinfo(NI_NUMERICHOST) and returns the formatted host in the 500 reply, disclosing the uninitialized sin6_scope_id (and flowinfo) to an authenticated client.

title: NPD: ((*resp = NULL, /vol1/1000/mygoldmine-benchmark/2026-11-17/targets/pure-ftpd/src/log_pam.c, 80, -1), ValueLabel.SRC)
label: FP
reason: PAM_conv is only installed as the libpam conversation callback in PAM_conversation, and pam_start()/pam_authenticate() call it with a valid struct pam_response ** per the PAM API. No in-tree caller passes NULL, so the report's premise that resp can be NULL is unsupported and the NPD is not reachable.

title: IPv6 EPRT error reply discloses uninitialized stack memory
label: TP
reason: Same root cause as strix:pure-ftpd:vuln-0002: an uninitialized sockaddr_storage scope/flowinfo field is passed to getnameinfo() in the EPRT FXP-mismatch reply, leaking stale stack bytes to an authenticated client.

title: PureDB IPv6 deny rules are silently discarded by colon-delimited record parsing
label: TP
reason: Same root cause as strix:pure-ftpd:vuln-0001: unescaped colons in an IPv6 deny literal shift the positional PureDB fields so the deny column is empty and access_ip_check() permits the login.

title: NLST/MLSD/MLST/MDTM/SIZE bypass the -X dot-file read policy
label: TP
reason: Same root cause as mygoldmine:pure-ftpd:NORM-PATH-001: listing/stat handlers process client paths without checknamesanity(), so enabling -X does not prevent enumeration of dot directories or metadata access to dot files.
